question: I’m researching species that became invasive after people who kept them as pets released them. There’s a certain species of fish that was popularized as a pet by being the main character of the movie Finding Nemo. According to the USGS, where was this fish found as a nonnative species, before the year 2020? I need the answer formatted as the five-digit zip codes of the places the species was found, separated by commas if there is more than one place.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Task: Find the USGS-documented nonnative occurrence(s) of the fish popularized by Finding Nemo (clownfish, Amphiprion ocellaris) before 2020 and return the relevant ZIP code(s) only. Team: WebSurfer (web access), Assistant (reasoning), FileSurfer (local/file ops if needed). Plan: 1) Use USGS NAS database to locate occurrence records for Amphiprion ocellaris pre-2020; 2) Extract precise location(s); 3) Map those locations to 5-digit ZIP(s); 4) Output only the ZIP code(s). WebSurfer, please search: site:nas.er.usgs.gov Amphiprion ocellaris occurrence USGS.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Search results show a USGS NAS species profile for Amphiprion ocellaris (clown anemonefish) with distribution/occurrence info. The snippet mentions at least one record on the Florida Gulf Coast (Pinellas County area). I can open the species page and check occurrence details and dates.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Open the USGS NAS species page for Amphiprion ocellaris and list the occurrence record(s) with locations and report dates. We need only records before 2020.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: On the USGS NAS Amphiprion ocellaris profile page: There is a nonindigenous occurrence in Florida, Gulf of Mexico, Pinellas County, near Anclote Key/Tarpon Springs area. The reported observation date is prior to 2020 (listed as an early 2000s report; the database notes aquarium release as a likely source). No additional U.S. occurrences are shown on this page before 2020.

history.name: Assistant
history.content:
Here are the candidate zip codes we derived from nearby coastal localities:
{
  'place': 'Anclote Key, near Tarpon Springs, Pinellas County, FL',
  'candidate_zips': [33767, 34689,],
  'confidence': 0.62,
}
Rationale: Anclote Key is offshore; nearest serviced ZIPs include Clearwater Beach (33767) to the south and Tarpon Springs (34689) to the north. Picking the closest may require a heuristic.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: The Assistant’s structured output failed to parse (non-JSON with single quotes and trailing comma). Defaulting to the first listed candidate to proceed. WebSurfer, quick verification: confirm that Clearwater Beach, FL is ZIP 33767.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Confirmed: Clearwater Beach, Florida uses ZIP code 33767 (USPS/City-Data references). Note: Anclote Key is offshore of Tarpon Springs (ZIP 34689) and north of Clearwater Beach (ZIP 33767).

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Given the parsing failure and proximity ambiguity for an offshore key, we will provide the verified ZIP 33767 as the nearest serviced locality on record. Only one pre-2020 USGS occurrence is indicated, so a single ZIP is expected.

mistake_reason: At step 5, the Assistant produced a malformed, non-compliant structured payload (used single quotes, included a trailing comma, and prefaced the data with conversational text). This FM-4.4 formatting error prevented the orchestrator from parsing the intended candidate ZIP list, triggering a fallback to the first listed item (33767). That led the team to select the wrong ZIP instead of the correct USGS-associated one (34689).
